Beállítom Évadnyitó Civil Akadémiára kaptak meghívót azok, akik feliratkoztak a Civil Összefogás Fórum (CÖF) hírlevelére, a szervezet a Civil Összefogás Közhasznú Alapítványával közösen ugyanis a 2026–27-es évadra is várja vendégeit – írta meg a 444. A meghívóban pedig nem is finomkodtak a korábbi Békemenetek szervezői: „Talán nem túlzás részünkről a megállapítás, hogy Magyarország felszámolás alatt áll. De lehet, hogy már nem is létezik” – kezdte a levelet a CÖF, majd egy kis filozofálással meg is indokolta, miért. „Mert mi is egy ország létalapja? Az erkölcse, a jogrendje és hagyománya, ha csak a fundamentum három alapvető elemére hivatkozok. Az erkölcse a hagyományból fakadóan rendezi az összehangolt társadalom működését, a jogi szabályozottság segítségére van. És e hármat számolja fel éppen a TiSza. És igen, lépésről-lépésre küzd a társadalmat legerőteljesebben meghatározó erkölcsös Magyarország ellen.” Hogy ne csak a levegőbe beszéljen, konkrét példákat is hozott a nemzethalál előjeleire a békepárti szervezet: küzd a vallásos közösségek ellen, gúnyolják, szidalmazzák a híveket, a papjaikat; a jogi védelem már nem létezik; nincs olyan jogszabály, legyen az akár alkotmányos, amit át ne lépnének. „Hát itt tartunk a TiSza 4. hónapjának működése idején. De ha felszámolnak mindent, őket sem fogja megvédeni sem erkölcsi akadály, sem jog. Ezt azért jó lenne észben tartaniuk” – szummázta levelében okfejtését a szervezet. Az elmúlt évek fideszes Békemeneteit is szervező CÖF–CÖKA 2024-ben azt írta, 1,257 milliárd forint támogatásból 1,256 milliárd magánemberek és vállalkozók adományaként folyt be hozzájuk. Részleteket nem közöltek. A Csizmadia által alapított CÖF–CÖKA májusban közölte, hogy felajánlja jogsegélyszolgálatát a jogalap nélküli támadások célpontjává váló civil támogatóinak, és feltehetően adományt is gyűjt majd a jogsegélyszolgálat finanszírozása érdekében. Az Átlátszó már 2018-ban arról írt, hogy a hazai energiaellátásért is felelős állami tulajdonú MVM a Civil Összefogás Fórumnak 508 millió forintot adott akkoriban, amiből például Brüsszelben szerveztek tüntetést Soros György ellen . A választásra egyébként hivatalosan is összeért a kormányzati üzeneteket propagáló Megafon, a Békemeneteket szervező CÖF és a Fidesz. A kormánypártok országos listájára több olyan elemző, influenszer és propagandista is felkerült, akik addig formálisan nem kötődtek a Fideszhez, de tavaly ősszel Folyami polgárnaszád néven kezdtek országjárásba. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6vg.text: Image source, EPA/Shutterstock Image caption, Albanese said it took "too long" for OpenAI to inform Australian officials of the breach in June By Harry Sekulich Â and Â Lana Lam ,Â Sydney Published 23 September 2026 Updated 2 minutes ago An artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI "infiltrated" an Australian government website in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has said. The agent hacked a statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare, Albanese said in New York on Wednesday, local time. He had a "very frank discussion" with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for taking "too long" to tell them about the breach, believed to be one of the world's first publicly reported AI-led hacks of a government website. OpenAI said it only became aware of the incident in August "during an ongoing review" of "misaligned model activity", and told Australian officials on 10 September. While the review is ongoing, OpenAI said in a statement that it is not believed any patient records were accessed. Albanese said the breach occurred in June this year, but OpenAI only informed Services Australia - the national hub directing users across government services - via email on 10 September. The agency contacted the relevant minister who passed on the information to the prime minister at the weekend. Albanese said he had also expressed "Australia's extreme concern about this incident" when he spoke to Altman and there will "obviously be legal consequences on it". Altman, the prime minister said, acknowledged there were "issues with protocols" at OpenAI. Albanese said the agent accessed both public and non-public files and a "forensic investigation" is under way to find out if other government systems were affected. The investigation will be led by the Australian Signals Directorate, the country's cybersecurity agency. The public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal which was hacked is administered by Services Australia . A spokesperson for OpenAI said in a statement: "We identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers, and available statistics for questions about Australia during an internal evaluation. "In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend," the statement continued. "The information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names." Albanese told reporters: "No personal information is believed to have been accessed at this stage, but investigations are ongoing. "Evidence currently available is there is no broader compromise to the Services Australia network. Nonetheless this situation is obviously unacceptable." Albanese declined to answer whether he raised the matter with US President Donald Trump during their face-to-face meeting on Tuesday night in New York, where world leaders have gathered for the UN General Assembly. Australia was one of 22 countries that this month signed a joint statement calling for global oversight and guardrails for the development of AI , external . Cybersecurity experts say the incident should "ring some alarm bells" for governments around the world, given that AI agents are becoming more widely available for individual and commercial use. "I expect that these kinds of attacks will keep occurring. They'll grow in severity and in frequency," Dr Hammond Pearce, senior lecturer at the University of New South Wales Institute for Cyber Security, told the BBC. Earlier this year, OpenAI revealed a group of AI agents it had been testing had escaped from their controls and secretly worked together to hack another tech firm named Hugging Face. The Hugging Face incident showed what can happen when an AI agent is not "well behaved", Dr Rob Nicholls, Senior Research Associate of AI regulation and policy at the University of Sydney, told the BBC. AI agents are usually set a task with an objective and a set of parameters, he said. "The problem is that agents aren't human," Dr Nicholls continued. "When you give [the agents] a task, the most important thing for that agent is to achieve what that task has been set and the rules tend to be a secondary issue to the objective and that's where the problem comes in." https://www.eng.kavkaz-uzel.eu/articles/.text: Homepage / All news 20:29, 16 September 2026 Criticism from the Armenian side regarding the visits of diplomats to Karabakh met with objections in Azerbaijan. Foreign diplomats have the right to visit Karabakh as an internationally recognized territory of Azerbaijan, and the demands to condemn such trips are unfounded, Azerbaijani analysts stated. As reported by " Caucasian Knot ", on September 16, about 50 organizations and public figures from Armenia, Nagorno-Karabakh, and the diaspora called on diplomatic missions in Yerevan to provide a political and legal assessment of the trips of foreign representatives to Karabakh and not to participate in actions that, in the opinion of the authors of the appeal, could contribute to the international legitimization of Azerbaijan's policy regarding the region and its Armenian heritage. On September 14, Karabakh activists considered the visit of diplomats accredited in Azerbaijan as a legitimization of the destruction of Armenian cultural heritage. The trip took place on September 11 and 12: a delegation of 150 people representing 58 countries and nine international organizations visited Khankendi, Shusha, Agdere, and Kelbajar districts. The Azerbaijani side stated that this was the 22nd visit of the diplomatic corps to the region since 2020, and the participants of the trip were shown the progress of restoration work and the condition of historical and cultural heritage sites. Farhadoglu and Juvarly considered the claims regarding the visits of diplomats to be unfounded The negative reaction in Armenia to the visit of foreign diplomats to Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur and the demands for explanations are unfounded, believes Turan analytical service employee Tapdyg Farhadoglu . "Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur are internationally recognized territories of Azerbaijan, and Baku has the right to invite foreign diplomats to these regions. By the way, Armenia itself recognized the territorial integrity of Azerbaijan in a number of international documents, including the Washington Declaration adopted last August, and the peace treaty that was initialed at the same time," he said to a correspondent of "Caucasian Knot". Foreign diplomats have previously visited territories that came under Azerbaijan's control as a result of the hostilities in 2020 and 2023, but such a strong reaction in Armenia did not occur, Farhadoglu pointed out. He linked the current reaction to the large composition of the delegation and the presence of ambassadors from countries that are traditionally considered supportive of Armenia in Yerevan, primarily France. After the 2020 war , the ambassadors of the co-chairing countries of the Minsk Group of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) refrained from traveling to Karabakh. Now, according to Farhadoglu, the situation has changed: the conflict is over, Armenia and Azerbaijan have initialed a peace agreement, economic ties are developing between the countries, Azerbaijan supplies fuel to Armenia and provides its communications for the transit of goods from Kazakhstan and Russia, and the Minsk Group of the OSCE has been dissolved . "In this situation, foreign diplomats have neither legal nor moral grounds to refuse to visit the regions of Azerbaijan affected by the conflict. Moreover, according to international law, they are obliged to respect the laws and sovereign rights of the host country," Farhadoglu said. The pragmatic interests of states also contribute to the development of their relations with Azerbaijan, which plays an increasingly active role in regional cooperation not only in the South Caucasus but also in Central Asia and partially in the Middle East. He named the goals of the diplomatic corps visit as demonstrating the scale of restoration work in the territories affected by the war and drawing attention to landmine contamination, Farhadoglu noted. The analyst also disagreed with accusations of "destruction" and "appropriation" of Armenian historical and cultural heritage. The medieval Christian monuments of the region, including the Gandzasar and Khudavang monasteries, he associated with the culture of Caucasian Albania. According to him, the Albanian church existed until the 19th century, and in 1836, the Holy Synod of the Russian Empire abolished it , after which the property and churches were transferred to the Armenian church. Disputes over the cultural heritage of Karabakh regularly become the subject of discussions on social networks. Thus, on June 29, participants in the discussion argued about the possible demolition of the monument "We are our mountains" and the impact of such a decision on Armenian-Azerbaijani peace negotiations. On March 18, a publication calling to preserve the Armenian heritage of Karabakh gained more than a thousand comments, in which users exchanged mutual accusations of vandalism and debated the need to involve the international community. "The existence of Caucasian Albania and its historical heritage is a well-known fact in world historical science," Farhadoglu said. Azerbaijani historical and cultural heritage in Armenia, according to Farhadoglu, is presented as Persian. "All Azerbaijani-Turkic historical heritage in Armenia is presented as "Persian". The only surviving Azerbaijani mosque in modern Armenia – the Blue Mosque in Yerevan – is presented as Persian, although it was built by the Yerevan khan of the Turkic dynasty. All Azerbaijani cemeteries have been destroyed in Armenia," the analyst noted. The international community has accepted the post-conflict realities of the region, he continued. According to the analyst, the South Caucasus can become a bridge for the development of transport communications between the East and the West, and European states are interested in regional projects in the fields of infrastructure, transport, energy, agriculture, and technology. "Therefore, the narratives about "Armenian Karabakh" are supported only by Armenian diaspora organizations and their lobbying groups," Farhadoglu pointed out. Christian cultural-historical and religious monuments of Karabakh belong to Albanian heritage, noted member of the Azerbaijani National Public Committee for Eurointegration Togrul Juvarly . According to him, Armenian cultural and religious monuments in the region appeared after the mass resettlement of Armenians from Persia and Ottoman Turkey to the South Caucasus after the region was conquered by the Russian Empire in the early 19th century. "Subsequently, many Albanian monuments were Armenianized <…>. Now they are being returned to their original appearance. All cultural and religious monuments are under state protection, including Armenian ones. In particular, the "Kazanchi" church was restored in Shusha," Juvarly told a correspondent of "Caucasian Knot". According to Juvarly, objects built in violation of the laws of Azerbaijan, architectural and urban planning norms may be subject to demolition. Claims regarding the visit of foreign diplomats to Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur are also unfounded, Juvarly believes. He pointed out that no state recognized the unrecognized republic that existed in Karabakh, and Armenia in 2022 in Prague recognized the territorial integrity of Azerbaijan, supporting the settlement based on the Almaty Declaration on the establishment of the Commonwealth of Independent States. In 2025, according to him, Armenia and Azerbaijan mutually recognized each other in the Washington documents. According to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations of 1961, the movement of accredited diplomats on the territory of the host state is regulated by the authorities of that state, Juvarly pointed out. "Therefore, any claims against both Azerbaijan and the countries whose diplomats participated in the trip are completely unfounded," he concluded. Social media users debated the legality of diplomats' visits to Karabakh A post stating that Armenian activists called on diplomats to condemn their colleagues' visits to Karabakh was published today on the "Caucasian Knot" Facebook page*, which has about 164,000 users. As of 20:25 MSK, this post received 15 user reactions and 29 comments. Users debated the legality of diplomats' visits and the status of the region. "The goal of these actions, organized by the highest political leadership of Azerbaijan, is to legitimize in every sense the de-Armenization of this historically Armenian region. Azerbaijan is conducting a policy of changing the historical and cultural heritage of Armenians in Nagorno-Karabakh, simply physically and informationally destroying it," stated Karen Babayan . "It is high time to recognize and understand that "the impressions of the international acceptability of the current situation" – everything that happens, happens within the internationally recognized borders of Azerbaijan, recognized by the world community, to which they appeal," noted Tofik Abbasov . "I urge the leadership of Azerbaijan to demand that diplomats from different countries not visit the city of Gafan and the entire Basarkechar region of Western Azerbaijan," wrote Turan Camal . Gafan is the current city of Kapan in the Syunik region of Armenia, Basarkechar is the former name of the current Vardenis. https://sana.sy/en/economic/2346023/.text: Syrian Chargé d'Affaires in Bucharest Anas Badawi meets with President of the Romanian Senate Mircea Abrudean to discuss economic, trade, and parliamentary cooperation, Sept. 25, 2026. Photo: SANA Bucharest, Sept. 25 (SANA) Chargé d’Affaires of the Syrian Embassy in Romania Anas Badawi met Friday with President of the Romanian Senate Mircea Abrudean in Bucharest to discuss strengthening political, economic, and trade relations between the two nations. In a statement posted on X, the Syrian Embassy reported that discussions focused on deepening political dialogue and expanding trade mechanisms to support Syria’s current economic recovery , leveraging more than seven decades of historic diplomatic relations. The meeting covered plans to organize an official visit by a Romanian parliamentary delegation to Syria during the first half of next year. Both sides also reviewed ongoing initiatives by the Romanian Chamber of Commerce to encourage investment, improve Syria’s business environment, and mobilize Syrian and Romanian expatriate communities to drive economic cooperation . The talks build on preliminary diplomatic engagements held in July, when Badawi met with Romanian Chamber of Commerce President Mihai Daraban and members of the Syrian Businessmen Council in Romania to lay the groundwork for upcoming joint business forums and trade delegations. https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.text: NEW DELHI: Satellite intelligence provider ICEYE and telecom equipment maker Nokia have partnered to develop secure and sovereign broadband low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications systems for governments, according to a joint statement.The first communications satellites developed under the initiative are scheduled for launch in 2028, targeting missions across national defence, border security, emergency services, and disaster response.Under the partnership, participating nations will retain complete ownership and control of satellites, ground segments, and terminals, leveraging European technology to establish secure communications infrastructure.The agreement comes as defence forces, first responders, and civil authorities face risks of losing access to critical command systems when terrestrial networks are disrupted or compromised.The jointly developed satellite infrastructure will deliver targeted, high-throughput, and low-latency connectivity over priority mission areas, complementing existing military and commercial networks rather than replacing them.The collaboration brings together ICEYE's experience in sovereign satellite missions with Nokia's expertise in secure networking technology and its expanding defence portfolio.By integrating satellites, ground infrastructure, and ruggedised end-user terminals, ICEYE will extend its sovereign intelligence from space business model directly into satellite communications.ICEYE noted that nations require full ownership and control over communications systems without relying on the terms of service of foreign commercial operators."Together with Nokia, we are building on our proven space intelligence expertise and delivering sovereign, high-performance satellite communications," said Rafal Modrzewski, chief executive officer and co-founder at ICEYE.Modrzewski added that ICEYE delivered Poland its own radar satellite system in under a year, noting the partnership with Nokia will enable a similar deployment speed for satellite communications."Sovereign operations depend on the ability to sense, decide and act in real time. Physical AI makes that possible, but only with secure, resilient connectivity across land, sea, air and space. By bringing together Nokia's trusted networks with ICEYE's proven sovereign space capabilities, we will deliver a satellite communications capability-complementing existing terrestrial networks and giving nations the situational awareness, connectivity, and control they need to operate with confidence in contested environments across all domains," said Justin Hotard, president and chief executive officer at Nokia.
